> **Lens**: Read the log the way the harness executed it, not the way it was typed.
> State that the tool keeps between calls is part of every call's meaning.

## Relates to

- Extends [ADR-0022](0022-record-kind-catalogue-and-skill-coverage.md) (the record's status line says "refines"; its detection rule)
- Extends [ADR-0023](0023-turn-boundaries-skill-ignore-and-replay.md) (the record's status line says "refines"; replay re-annotates under the new rule)

## Problem

### Symptom

0022 detects that a tool call touched a skill file when the call's arguments contain `<skill>/<path>`.
0022's consequences already named the blind spot: a file reached through something the harness resolves itself is a miss.
The first paid run of the second suite (`eval_dual_density`, Claude Opus 5, 2026-08-23) hit that blind spot squarely.
The agent did `cd …/skills/mermaidjs-diagrams && cat SKILL.md`, then `cat resources/diagram_organization.md`, then `bun run scripts/mermaid_complexity.ts …`.
It relied on the one thing Claude Code's `Bash` tool promises and Codex's `exec` does not.
The shell is persistent, so a `cd` in one call is the working directory of the next.

### Pain point

None of those commands contains the literal `mermaidjs-diagrams/SKILL.md`.
The run was scored `skill 0/18 loaded 0/4 run`.
The grader's "did the agent run the gates it was told are mandatory" check failed, and $1.95 bought a wrong verdict.
Replaying the same log under a detector that follows the shell gives `7/18 loaded 3/4 run`, and re-grading the unchanged workspace passes every check.

## Decision

### The lens

- **Given**: The session log holds everything needed to do better.
  The harness announces when it moves the shell back, with `Shell cwd was reset to <dir>` inside the tool result.
  Codex carries an explicit `workdir` on every exec, and the result records the workspace the run started in.
- **We prefer**: Modelling the shell's working directory per result, and rewriting relative tokens before matching.
  That is preferred over matching the literal text of a command as typed.
- **Because**: State that the tool keeps between calls is part of every call's meaning.
  Reading the log any other way buys wrong verdicts with real money.
- **Unless**: a `cd` target cannot be known, in which case the working directory is unknown until the next absolute `cd` or reset.
  An unknowable target is `~`, `$VAR`, or a bare `cd`.

### In practice

- `annotate` models the shell per result.
  The working directory starts at the run's workspace.
  A `cd` segment in a persistent-shell tool call (`Bash`) moves it for the rest of that command and for the calls after it.
  A `Shell cwd was reset to <dir>` in a tool result moves it back.
  A `cd` whose target cannot be known makes it unknown until the next absolute `cd` or reset.
  An unknowable target is `~`, `$VAR`, or a bare `cd`.
  Codex's exec tools run each call at their own `workdir` and a `cd` there does not persist.
- Detection itself is unchanged.
  A shell command is split at `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines.
  A segment counts when its working directory is the skill's root or a directory under it.
  In such a segment, each relative token that looks like a file is rewritten to `<skill>/<sub>/<token>`.
  A token looks like a file when it contains a `.` or a `/`, and is not already qualified.
  It must also not start with `/`, `-`, `$` or a redirection.
  The rewritten command is then matched by 0022's rule.
  `bun run scripts/gate.ts` after `cd <skill>` becomes `bun run <skill>/scripts/gate.ts`, and is a run.
  `cat SKILL.md` becomes `cat <skill>/SKILL.md`, and is a load.
  `echo done` stays a word.
- The shell state lives inside `annotate`, derived from `result.calls` in order.
  The plugin's live path and replay therefore produce the same coverage from the same log, and nothing is shared between results.

## Consequences

### Pros

- The plugin's live path and replay produce the same coverage from the same log, and nothing is shared between results.

### Cons

- Coverage from a captured log can change when the detector improves.
  That is what replay is for, and it is why a verdict that depends on coverage should be re-graded rather than re-bought.
- Replay keeps the verdict a cell was given at the time.
  A run scored under the old rule therefore still reads `fail` in the history, until it is re-run or a regrade step exists.
  The report's raw records beside the coverage table show the difference.
- The model is a heuristic over text.
  A `cd` inside a subshell or a function is taken as persisting.
  A heredoc's body is split like a command, so its tokens are rewritten but match no file.
  A token with a `.` in a segment under the skill is counted when it happens to name a real skill file.
  Each of those errs toward counting a file.
  That is the cheaper error for a tool whose purpose is to show the decision paths an agent never took.
